SELL_CARDS: deprioritised by the owner (2026-11-17), but note it is NOT automatic: this is the in-game sale, an action that costs a turn, and the agent never takes it (100% stop, 319 936 rows). The end-of-game cleanup is a different turn. Revisit when cards are the bottleneck - at 3 MC per card it is the only way to turn a dead card into money while actions still exist.
SELL_CARDS_LAST_ROUND: forced cleanup, not a decision with value: SellExtraCardsState offers it only when player.getNextTurn() == null and the hand is above MAX_HAND_SIZE_LAST_ROUND = 10, at 3 MC per card. The money arrives after the last turn and money is not scored (ScoreBreakdown has no MC term), so the ~9.7 MC it raises per game is dead. The measured +0.18 correlation with the margin is the hand size, not the sale.
MULLIGAN: Measured 18/11: the critic cannot gate the mulligan in either formulation - with the engine's replacement draw the gate found 91.8% of removals 'free' (mean 6.58 discards of 10), and with a deterministic 'hand minus this card' afterstate 91.6% (mean 9.10), because V prefers a smaller hand and a mulligan does not shrink it. A fixed count is not the answer either (2 cards: 63.75%, 5 cards: 60.25% against 63.93% at 0). The policy must learn it from explored games weighted by outcomes (MULLIGAN:0.9 gives ~5 discards of 10); the card CHOICE stays with the critic's ranking.
